exercises.prompt: Fill in ( a ) to ( d ) with the four layers, broadest first.
exercises.promptAr: كمّل ( أ ) لـ ( د ) بالأربع طبقات، الأوسع الأول.
exercises.passage: ( a ) is the broad field. Inside it is ( b ), which learns patterns from data. Inside that is ( c ), which uses neural networks. Built on top of it is ( d ), which makes new text and images.

exercises.prompt: Write ✓ if the statement is true, ✗ if it is false.
exercises.promptAr: اكتب ✓ لو الجملة صح، و ✗ لو غلط.
statements: Machine learning is one of the technologies that makes AI work.
Deep learning is a completely different technology from machine learning.
Generative AI is a technology that uses deep learning to generate new data.
AI and machine learning have the same meaning.

exercises.prompt: Match each description to the most appropriate term.
Machine learning learns patterns from data. What two things does it use those patterns for?
exercises.promptAr: الـ machine learning بيتعلم أنماط من الداتا. بيستخدمها في حاجتين إيه؟

exercises.prompt: Explain what a neural network is.
Sort the examples into Classifies or Generates.
exercises.promptAr: قسّم الأمثلة: بيصنّف ولا بيولّد حاجة جديدة.

exercises.prompt: Write ✓ if the statement is true, ✗ if it is false.

statements: AI and machine learning have the same meaning.
ChatGPT can be an example of generative AI.
A spam filter is an example of generative AI.

exercises.prompt: Write A, B or C: A = machine learning, B = deep learning, C = generative AI.
exercises.promptAr: اكتب A أو B أو C: A machine learning، B deep learning، C generative AI.

exercises.prompt: A farmer uses AI to identify healthy and diseased crops in photographs. Explain what it needs to learn from and one reason its judgment might be wrong.
exercises.promptAr: المزارع عايز AI يفرّق بين زرع سليم ومريض في الصور. اشرح يتعلم من إيه، وليه ممكن حكمه يغلط.

exercises.prompt: Analyse the relationship between AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI. Use nested categories and give one example of each.
exercises.promptAr: حلّل علاقة AI وmachine learning وdeep learning وgenerative AI كطبقات جوه بعض، وادّي مثال لكل واحد.

exercises.prompt: Classify each: spam sorting, pedestrian recognition in autonomous driving, and generating an image from text.
exercises.promptAr: صنّف كل واحدة: spam sorting، تمييز المشاة في عربية ذاتية، وعمل صورة من text.

exercises.prompt: Answer with the correct term for each.

questions.q: The general term, given as a two-letter abbreviation, for technologies that reproduce or perform intelligent human behaviour on a computer.
The learning technology that makes AI work by learning patterns from data to make predictions and judgments.
The advanced technology within machine learning that uses neural networks.
The AI technology that uses deep learning to generate new data.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct option in each.
exercises.promptAr: اختر الإجابة الصح في كل واحدة.

questions.q: (1) Which shows the correct relationship?  A: AI > Deep Learning > Machine Learning > Generative AI   B: Machine Learning > AI > Generative AI > Deep Learning   C: AI > Machine Learning > Deep Learning > Generative AI   D: Generative AI > Deep Learning > Machine Learning > AI
(2) Which is NOT an appropriate example of generative AI?  A: ChatGPT   B: Image generation AI   C: Spam filter   D: Audio generation AI

exercises.prompt: Generative AI can produce text that sounds plausible but is factually incorrect — a hallucination. Explain why it is dangerous to hand such output in as a school report as it is, and state what you should do instead.
exercises.promptAr: الـ generative AI ممكن يطلّع كلام شكله مقنع بس غلط — ده اسمه hallucination. اشرح ليه خطر تسلّم الكلام ده كتقرير مدرسي زي ما هو، وقول تعمل إيه بدل كده.

exercises.prompt: Generative AI can create text, images and audio. Suggest one genuinely helpful use, and one possible misuse, and say what makes the difference between them.
exercises.promptAr: الـ generative AI بيعمل نص وصور وصوت. اقترح استخدام مفيد فعلًا، واستخدام ضار، وقول إيه اللي بيفرّق بينهم.

exercises.prompt: Research task. Find one documented case where a generative AI gave an answer that sounded correct but was wrong. Record where you found it — a news article, an official report, or your own tested prompt with a screenshot. Do not rely on an example given in class.
exercises.promptAr: مهمة بحث. دوّر على حالة موثقة لـ generative AI قال إجابة شكلها صح وطلعت غلط. سجّل مصدرك — خبر، تقرير رسمي، أو تجربة عملتها بنفسك بصورة. متعتمدش على مثال اتقال في الحصة.

2: ✓ — correct, machine learning is one of the technologies that makes AI work
✗ — deep learning is an advanced kind of machine learning, not a separate field
✗ — AI is the broad field; machine learning is one technology inside it
ANSWERS.3: AI reproduces or performs intelligent human behavior on a computer; examples include speech recognition, image recognition or translation.
ANSWERS.4: Patterns, to make predictions and judgments.
ANSWERS.6: A system modeled after the brain’s nerve cells; connected components learn from data and make complex judgments.
ANSWERS.9: It has too few relevant examples from which to learn the pattern.
ANSWERS.10: It needs photographs/data of healthy and diseased crops; it may be wrong when the data has too few or unrepresentative examples.
ANSWERS.11: Output that sounds plausible but is factually incorrect; it must be checked before being used as a report answer.
ANSWERS.12: Machine learning; deep learning; generative AI.
14: (1) C — AI > Machine Learning > Deep Learning > Generative AI
(2) C — a spam filter classifies email; it does not generate new data

points: A hallucination reads as confidently as a correct answer, so the reader cannot tell.
The student is responsible for what they hand in, not the tool.
An error passed on as fact can mislead whoever reads the report.
What to do instead: check every fact against the textbook or another reliable source before using it.
15.marking: 2 marks for why it is dangerous, 2 for a concrete checking step. Naming 'hallucination' alone is not an explanation.

16.marking: One helpful use, one misuse, and a stated distinction. Look for the distinction — most answers give two examples and never say what separates them.
16.example: Helpful: drafting practice questions to revise from. Misuse: submitting generated text as your own work. The difference is whether the output is checked and whether authorship is honest.

17.marking: Requires a named source the teacher can check. An example repeated from the lesson scores zero for the research part. Accept a screenshot of the student's own tested prompt.
